Bargaining is completely inappropriate here, young man.
But this is a very expensive restaurant!
I know this fine restaurant perfectly well.
The administrator will throw you out into the street immediately.
In a decent suit nobody will recognize me.
And what if you accidentally ruin someone else's clothes?
I promise to behave extremely neatly.
Where exactly are our missing truffles hidden?
You will receive the truffles right after lunch.
The Chef will get very angry if he finds out the truth.
Then wish me bon appétit, Konstantin.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'administrator', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.text: Входишь сразу налево, к администратору. Там сидит такой Лисицын.
examples.trans: You go in and turn straight left, to the administrator. A fellow named Lisitsyn sits there.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: They have to be washed carefully by hand.
Put the glasses carefully on the table.

examples.text: Ты что, Аркашка? Это же югославские вещи! Их аккуратно руками надо стирать.
examples.trans: Are you crazy, Arkashka? These are Yugoslavian things! They have to be washed carefully by hand.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'appetite', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('!') (= Enjoy your meal!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.en: to lead, to guide, to drive
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to lead', forming an aspectual pair with 'повести'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Вы как маленькая себя ведёте = You're behaving like a little girl

examples.trans: You're behaving like a little girl.

examples.text: Лидия Алексеевна, успокойтесь, пожалуйста! Вы как маленькая себя ведёте.
examples.trans: Lydia Alexeyevna, calm down, please! You're behaving like a little girl.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

выгнать.gloss: to kick out, to evict, to drive out

meanings.en: to kick out, to drive out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'гнать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to kick out', forming an aspectual pair with 'выгонять'.

examples.text: Для тебя она добрая. А меня она выгонит!
examples.trans: She's kind to you. But she'll kick me out!

examples.text: Значит, меня не выгонят со службы?
examples.trans: Does that mean I won't be fired from service?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'where'.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: + infinitive: давай убирать = let's clean up
Secondary conversational sense ('come on') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('bye, see you') (casual goodbye) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'платить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to pay', forming an aspectual pair with 'платить'.

examples.trans: I have already paid for dinner.

examples.text: И денег я тебе заплачу. В десять раз больше!
examples.trans: And I'll pay you money. Ten times more!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.
Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
Secondary conversational sense ('namely') (а именно = namely) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'портить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to spoil', forming an aspectual pair with 'портить'.

examples.text: А я испорчу отношения с будущим мэром.
examples.trans: And I'll ruin my relationship with the future mayor.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'suit', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('costume, outfit') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: This is my wedding suit, actually!

meanings.en: extremely, exceptionally, to a high degree
meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'extremely'.

examples.trans: It was an extremely dangerous experiment.

meanings.note: молодой человек = young man (polite address)

examples.text: Молодой человек, как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?

examples.text: Молодой человек, а как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'inappropriate' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: This loud argument is inappropriate here.

examples.text: Торг здесь совершенно неуместен, молодой человек.
examples.trans: Bargaining is completely inappropriate here, young man.

meanings.note: needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'lunch', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Всё, давайте. У меня перерыв на обед.
examples.trans: Alright, carry on. I have my lunch break.

meanings.note: + dative of the person: обещать вам

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: singular in Russian, unlike English

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'желать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to wish', forming an aspectual pair with 'желать'.

examples.trans: The waiter wished the guest a pleasant evening.

examples.text: Тогда пожелайте мне приятного аппетита, Константин.
examples.trans: Then wish me bon appétit, Konstantin.
Be sure to wish them bon appétit.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get, to receive', paired with 'получать'.

examples.text: А кто их получит? Те, кто сидит повыше?
examples.trans: And who will get it? The people who sit higher up?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'after' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Я прекрасно понимаю = I understand perfectly
Secondary conversational sense ('wonderful!') (as a reply) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нет, лучше так: все говорят, а я делаю! Прекрасно.
examples.trans: No, better like this: everyone talks, while I do! Excellent.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, wonderful').

examples.text: Посмотри, какой у нас город прекрасный. Озёра, луга.
examples.trans: Look what a beautiful town we have. Lakes, meadows.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'decent' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: He put on a decent clean suit.

examples.text: В приличном костюме меня никто не узнает.
examples.trans: In a decent suit nobody will recognize me.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'pleasant' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('!') (= Enjoy your meal!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'missing', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: The cooks were looking for the missing ingredients.

examples.text: Где именно спрятаны наши пропавшие трюфели?
examples.trans: Where exactly are our missing truffles hidden?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

разозлиться.gloss: to get angry, to lose one's temper

meanings.en: to get angry, to become furious
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'озлиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to get angry', forming an aspectual pair with 'злиться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Уйди от меня! Я сейчас разозлюсь!
examples.trans: Get away from me! I'm going to get angry right now!
He got very angry at his friend.

examples.text: Шеф сильно разозлится, если узнает правду.
examples.trans: The Chef will get very angry if he finds out the truth.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'strongly'.

examples.trans: The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: а вы случайно не...? = are you by any chance...?
Secondary conversational sense ('by accident, unintentionally') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Are you by any chance Samson?

examples.text: Здравствуйте! Извините, а вы случайно не Самсон?
examples.trans: Hello! Excuse me, are you by any chance Samson?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'completely'.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.
This is a completely new car.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города. И предложение у меня к вам такое.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town. And my offer to you is this.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'прятать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hide', paired with 'прятать'.

examples.text: Мэр куда-то спрятал деньги. Местные чиновники не могут собрать нужную сумму.
examples.trans: The mayor has hidden the money somewhere. The local officials can't put together the sum they need.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.
Secondary conversational sense ('then, in that case') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'bargaining', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: In this situation haggling is out of place.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'truffle', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Шеф, дорогой, а трюфели тебе надо?
examples.trans: Chef, my dear, do you need truffles?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to recognise; to find out', paired with 'узнавать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to find out, to learn') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'll find out where he is.
You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

meanings.note: на улице = out on the street / outside
на улице холодно = it's cold outside

examples.text: На Московской улице перевернули ящики с мусором.
examples.trans: On Moskovskaya Street someone tipped over the rubbish bins.
There are reporters out on the street!

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Secondary conversational sense ('people') (plural люди, a different word) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: neuter чужое as a noun = other people's things
Secondary conversational sense ('stranger's, foreign') (чужой человек = a stranger) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking?

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса, да?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking, yes?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
